title: Impact Crusher

introduction.definition: A horizontal shaft impact (HSI) crusher breaks material by impact rather than compression. A fast-turning rotor with blow bars strikes the falling feed and throws it against impact aprons (curtains). Rocks shatter along natural weaknesses, giving a well-shaped (cubical) product. The gap between the rotor and the aprons controls the product size.
key_points: High reduction ratio and good shape
introduction.summary: A horizontal shaft impact crusher breaks rock by impact. Blow bars on a fast rotor hit the falling rock and hurl it against impact aprons; it shatters along natural weaknesses, giving cubical product. The apron gap sets product size.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Finer product with higher rotor speed and smaller apron gap; wear rate rises steeply with abrasiveness and speed.

wear.title: Apron and blow-bar wear
wear.description: The lower (secondary) apron sees finer, faster material and a closer gap, so it wears most (purple). Blow bars wear on their leading edge; they are turned end-for-end or reversed, and replaced in opposite pairs to keep the rotor balanced. Worn bars and aprons open the effective gap and coarsen the product.

foundation: Mount on a massive reinforced-concrete foundation or steel structure designed for the crusher's dynamic loads (maker's load data); use anti-vibration mounts where specified.
Allow crane access and lay-down space for liner and wear-part changes.
alignment: Align motor and crusher sheaves or coupling; set V-belt tension to the maker's figure.
Set the closed-side setting (CSS) or gap with the maker's gauge/lead-ball method.
piping: Feed with a controlled feeder (choke or regulated feed as designed); avoid segregated or one-sided feed.
Fit a tramp-metal magnet or metal detector ahead of the crusher and dust extraction at transfer points.
Lubrication system: connect oil supply/return, cooler and filter; check flow and pressure switches.
commissioning: Check lubrication flows and temperatures before starting; run empty to check direction, vibration and current.
Introduce feed gradually; measure product size and adjust the setting; record power draw as a baseline.

routine.task: Check vibration and blow-bar wear through inspection doors.

overhaul.task: Turn/replace blow bars (in balanced pairs) and liners; replace bearings.

causes: Unequal blow-bar wear or mismatched bars

safety: Lock out and pin the rotor before opening; flying debris hazard — keep doors closed when running.

script.narration: This module introduces the Impact Crusher.
A horizontal shaft impact (HSI) crusher breaks material by impact rather than compression.
A fast-turning rotor with blow bars strikes the falling feed and throws it against impact aprons (curtains).
Rocks shatter along natural weaknesses, giving a well-shaped (cubical) product.
Typical applications include limestone and softer rock crushing; recycling concrete and asphalt; secondary crushing for cubical aggregate.

video_tutorials.title: Impact Crusher — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Impact Crusher.
Check vibration and blow-bar wear through inspection doors.
Measure and adjust apron gaps.
Turn/replace blow bars (in balanced pairs) and liners; replace bearings.
Watch for rotor imbalance: high vibration. Common cause: unequal blow-bar wear or mismatched bars.
Watch for product too coarse: oversize. Common cause: worn bars/aprons, gap too large.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
